question.problem:
Let ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{148}$ be a random sample of size $n=148$ from a population with a population mean $\mu =98$ and population standard deviation $\sigma =74.$ Find an approximation for the probability that the sample mean is greater than $95.$

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ | $\,0.09\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-0.5\,$ | $\,0.2843\,$ | $\,0.2810\,$ | $\,0.2776\,$ |
| $\,-0.4\,$ | $\,0.3192\,$ | $\,0.3156\,$ | $\,0.3121\,$ |
| $\,-0.3\,$ | $\,0.3557\,$ | $\,0.3520\,$ | $\,0.3483\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Suppose that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a population with a population mean $\mu $ and population standard deviation $\sigma .$ The central limit theorem (or CLT) states that for sufficiently large $n,$ the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ can be approximated as 

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

In our case, we have

$$
n=148,\,\mu =98,\,\sigma =74.
$$

Therefore, by the CLT, we have that the distribution of the sample mean can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}) \\  & ∼N\,(98,\frac{{74}^{2}}{148}) \\  & ∼N(98,37).\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find $P(\overset{―}{X}>95).$ So, we convert $\overset{―}{X}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}>95) & =P(Z>\frac{95-98}{\sqrt{37}}) \\  & =P(Z>-\frac{3}{\sqrt{37}}) \\  & ≈P(Z>-0.49)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the complement of the normal distribution, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z>-0.49) & =1-P(Z<-0.49) \\  & =1-Φ(-0.49).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.49)=0.3121.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}>95) & =1-Φ(-0.49) \\  & =1-0.3121 \\  & =0.6879.\end{aligned}
$$
